neighbours.label: asking whether something has happened lately: questions put to 'you' about a specific recent episode ('Have you taken any…', 'Did you eat anything…'), at the slot where 'recently/lately' fits
fire: Before we begin, have you had any headaches or dizzy spells?
The nurse asked, "Have you changed your diet or started any new pills?"
Quick question: did you notice anything strange about the car?
So tell me, have you been working longer hours than usual?
For the form I need to know, have you visited a farm or handled animals?
The officer leaned in and asked, "Did you see anyone leaving the building?"
By the way, have you heard anything from your brother?
The vet wanted to know, has your cat been eating less or hiding?
quiet: Before we begin, headaches and dizzy spells are common at this altitude.
The nurse said, "A balanced diet works better than any pills."
Quick fact: every car of that model has a strange gearbox.
So remember, bakers work longer hours than most people.
For the form I need your name, your address and the name of the farm.
The officer leaned in and said, "Nobody leaves this building without a pass."
By the way, my brother lives two streets from here.
The vet explained that cats eat less and hide when they are in pain.

notes: Card: top examples are 'Have you had… any long trips', 'Have you seen a lynx', 'have travelled in the last 14 days', 'have been used'; output promotes ' recent', ' recently', ' lately', and the - pole peaks on ' in'/' most'/' more' before 'recent(ly)'. Probes: Have you… 0.63-0.83, Did you eat anything unusual 0.82, Will you be taking any long trips 0.56, declarative 'have been used' 0.46, habitual 'Do you sleep badly when…' 0.19. So it is wider than the present perfect; near misses here are habitual or timeless.
